matched_title: GET /pulls/:id no longer fetches fresh data from GitHub

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer fetches fresh data from GitHub
findings.rationale: The old handler attempted a live GitHub fetch on every GET and fell back to persisted data only on failure. The new handler always returns the persisted data without any GitHub call. Any caller that relied on the GET to return fresh data (e.g., e2e tests, CI runners, or the web client before the Refresh button is clicked) will now see stale data until they explicitly call `POST /pulls/:id/refresh`. This narrows the contract: freshness is no longer a side effect of reading.

matched_title: GET /pulls/:id no longer fetches fresh data from GitHub — silent staleness for existing callers

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer fetches fresh data from GitHub — silent staleness for existing callers
findings.rationale:
The old handler attempted to fetch the latest PR details from GitHub on every call (with a fallback to stored data on failure). The new handler always serves stored data without any freshness indicator. Any deployed caller that relied on the old behavior — for example, a CI runner polling for updated PR status, or an external consumer that expected fresh data — will now silently receive stale data. The response schema is unchanged, so no type error occurs; the regression is purely semantic and invisible to the caller.

**Compatible alternative:** Keep the old behavior as an opt-in via a query parameter (e.g., `GET /pulls/:id?refresh=true`) so existing callers can continue to get fresh data without code changes, or add a `last_refreshed_at` field to the response so callers can detect staleness and decide to call `POST /pulls/:id/refresh` if needed.

findings.title: POST /pulls/:id/refresh does not handle GitHub API errors — returns 500 instead of a structured error
findings.rationale: The new `POST /pulls/:id/refresh` endpoint calls `container.github()` and `gh.getPullRequest` without a try-catch. If no GitHub token is configured, or if the GitHub API is unreachable or rate-limited, the endpoint will throw an unhandled exception and return a generic 500 error. The old `GET` handler had a try-catch that logged a warning and fell back to stored data. The new endpoint should catch these errors and return a structured error response (e.g., `{ error: { code: 'GITHUB_UNAVAILABLE', message: '…' } }`) so the client can surface a meaningful message to the user.
